frontMatter.purpose:
At A Packaging Group, we recognize that our people are our most valuable asset, and we are committed to foster a positive and inclusive work environment where everyone can thrive. This manual outlines the policies, procedures, and guidelines that govern various aspects of employment within our organization. Through this we strive to ensure clarity, consistency, sustainability and fairness in our practices, while also promoting compliance with legal requirements and industry standards. We encourage all employees to familiarize themselves with the contents of this manual and to refer to it as needed for guidance on matters related to employment, workplace policies, and company culture. Hence we believe in achieving:
“ Excellence in Packaging by Empowering Sustainability”
Our Guiding Principle to inherit integrity, respect, fairness and foster a culture where every individual is valued, treated equitably, and empowered to uphold the highest ethical standards
This Policy applies to all employees of A Packaging, across all levels and all departments.

chapters.title: Dress Code
chapters.text:
- Employees are expected to maintain a neat and professional appearance at all times, regardless of the dress code. Any attire that is overly casual, revealing, or inappropriate for a business setting is not permitted.
- Days for Formal Dress: Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays
- Days for Informal Dress: Tuesdays and Thursdays
- Formal Attire
- Men: Business suits or dress pants with collared shirts, ties, and closed-toe dress shoes
- Women: Business suits, knee-length skirts or dress pants paired with blouses or professional tops, closed-toe shoes.
- Informal Attire
- Men: Dress pants or khakis with collared shirts or polo shirts, and casual shoes such as loafers or dressy sneakers
- Women: Casual skirts, dresses, or dress pants with blouses or informal tops, and comfortable yet presentable footwear.
## Business Etiquette
- Business Etiquette plays a crucial role in maintaining positive relationships with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders and reflects the professionalism of the company. Employees are expected to adhere to accepted norms of behavior in business settings, including punctuality, active listening, clear communication, and respect for cultural differences.
- This includes using appropriate language and tone in written and verbal communications, maintaining confidentiality when required, and representing the company with integrity and professionalism at all times.
## Confidentiality and Data Protection
- Confidentiality and Data Protection are paramount to safeguard sensitive information and maintain trust with customers, employees, and partners.
- Employees are required to handle confidential information with care and discretion, only disclosing it to authorized individuals on a need-to-know basis. This includes customer data, proprietary information, trade secrets, and any other sensitive data collected or used in the course of business.
- Employees must also comply with data protection laws and company policies regarding the collection, storage, and processing of personal data, both internally and externally. Violations of confidentiality and data protection policies may result in disciplinary action, legal consequences, and damage to the company's reputation.
## RECRUITMENT & ONBOARDING POLICY
## Purpose
The recruitment policy is designed to attract, select, and retain qualified individuals who align with the company's values, culture, and objectives. This policy outlines the procedures and guidelines for the recruitment process to ensure fairness, transparency, and efficiency in hiring practices.
## Scope
This Policy and Procedure applies to all hiring managers of A Packaging Group.
## Recruitment Process:
APackaging Group is committed to conducting all recruitment and selection processes in an open, transparent, and merit-based manner that ensures equal opportunity for all candidates, whether internal or external.
The company upholds a zero-tolerance policy toward any form of discrimination in hiring based on gender, race, ethnicity, color, religion, disability, nationality, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
To maintain fairness and inclusivity throughout the recruitment process, A Packaging Group has implemented the following measures:
## Transparent Job Postings:
All job openings are communicated publicly through appropriate internal and external channels, clearly outlining job requirements, qualifications, and selection criteria. Job descriptions are based solely on the skills, experience, and competencies necessary for the role, avoiding any language that could imply bias or discourage diverse applicants.

chapters.title: Standardized Recruitment Procedures:
chapters.text:
The company follows a structured, step-by-step recruitment process including application screening, interviews, and assessments. Each stage is guided by objective evaluation criteria, ensuring that decisions are made based on merit, capability, and organizational fit rather than personal preference or subjective bias.
## nclusive Candidate Shortlisting:
All applications are reviewed against predefined criteria. Candidate shortlists are compiled by HR in collaboration with hiring managers, ensuring consistency and avoiding unconscious bias. Where applicable, HR uses anonymized resume screening or diverse interview panels to promote impartial evaluation.
## Anti-Discrimination and Bias Training:
Recruiters, HR personnel, and hiring managers undergo periodic training on anti-discrimination laws, unconscious bias, and inclusive hiring practices. This ensures awareness of potential biases and reinforces adherence to fair hiring principles.
## Documentation and Audit Trail:
All recruitment decisions and evaluations are documented and stored for audit purposes. HR periodically reviews these records to ensure compliance with company policies and legal requirements, as well as to detect and correct any emerging patterns of bias or inconsistency.
## Grievance Channel for Recruitment Concerns:
Candidates who believe they have faced discrimination or unfair treatment during recruitment may file a complaint through the company’s grievance mechanism. All such complaints are handled promptly, confidentially, and without retaliation.

chapters.title: Onboarding:
chapters.text:
- Upon offer acceptance, HR will confirm the joining date with the candidate and hiring manager.
- New joiners will not be onboarded after the 25th of the month or on Thursdays/Fridays, except for urgent hirings.
- HR will notify relevant departments about new joiners asset requirements. Departments are responsible for arranging these before the joining date.
- On the joining date, HR will provide new joiners with welcome emails, necessary documentation, and induction schedules. All managers must conduct induction for new joiners as required.
## Age Verification:
- Candidates must be at least 18 years old for employment consideration.
- HR will verify candidates age through legal documentation discreetly and in compliance with laws. Records of age verification will be maintained as per data protection regulations and company policies. Any concerns about candidate age will be promptly addressed by HR.
- Discrimination based on age is prohibited. Instances of age-related bias should be reported and addressed. HR personnel involved in age verification will receive appropriate training on compliance and discrimination prevention.
## Confidentiality and Data Protection:
- All information obtained during the recruitment process will be treated with confidentiality and handled in accordance with data protection laws and company policies. Personal data of candidates will be used solely for recruitment purposes and will be securely stored and retained as per company guidelines.
## Continuous Improvement:
- At A packaging we are committed to continuously improve the recruitment process through feedback, evaluation, and ongoing review of recruitment practices.
- Feedback from candidates, hiring managers, and HR stakeholders will be solicited and considered to identify areas for enhancement and ensure a positive candidate experience.
## Compliance:
- This recruitment policy is in compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards governing employment practices.
- HR will regularly review and update the policy to ensure alignment with legal requirements and best practices in recruitment and selection.
## WORKING DAYS AND HOURS
## Purpose
To provide guidelines to employees on the working days and hours and applicable overtimes.
## Scope
This Policy and Procedure applies to all employees of A Packaging Group.
## Standard working days
- Employees are expected to work from Monday to Friday each week, unless otherwise specified by their employment contract or company policies.
- The standard workweek consists of five consecutive days, with weekends (Saturday and Sunday) designated as non-working days.
## Standard working hours:
- The standard working hours for full-time employees at A Packaging are from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with one hour allotted for lunch.
- This results in a total of 8 hours of work per day and 40 hours per week.
- However, specific working hours may vary depending on the nature of the job, departmental requirements, and any applicable legal regulations.
- Time Monitoring Procedure: Employee attendance and working hours are monitored through the company’s digital attendance system, where employees are required to clock in and clock out using biometric or RFID access at the beginning and end of their shift. The system automatically records total hours worked, late arrivals, early departures, and overtime. HR reviews these records monthly to ensure compliance with working hour policies and to address discrepancies, if any.
## Flexible Working Arrangements:
- A Packaging Group recognizes the importance of promoting work-life balance and may offer flexible working arrangements to eligible employees upon request and approval.
- Flexible working arrangements may include options such as flextime, compressed workweeks, telecommuting, or part-time schedules.
- Employees interested in exploring flexible working arrangements should discuss their needs with their supervisors and HR representatives to determine feasibility and eligibility.
## Absence within working hours
- In the event of an emergency or if a personal appointment during working hours is necessary, employees are required to promptly inform both their Reporting Manager and HR via email, specifying the reason for being late or out of the office.
- If leaving before the scheduled business hours closure, employees must submit an advance request to their Reporting Manager, with notification to HR.
- Approval from the Reporting Manager for early departure is mandatory.
## Overtime and Compensation:
- In cases where employees are required to work beyond their standard working hours, they may be eligible for overtime compensation in accordance with applicable labor laws and company policies.
- Overtime Calculation:
- Regular Rate of Pay: The regular rate of pay includes the employee's hourly rate for hourly workers or the weekly salary divided by the number of hours worked for salaried workers.

chapters.title: Leave Policy
chapters.text:
## Purpose
To provide guidelines to employees on the holidays and leaves available. This policy provides guidelines on sanctioning and availing the leave for vacation, personal emergencies, illness, and parenthood etc.
## Scope
This Policy and Procedure applies to all employees and covers all Leave entitlements.
## Leave types and Policy
- Vacation Leave: All full-time employees are eligible for vacation leave after completing 6 months of continuous service, Employees accrue vacation leave at a rate of 2 days per month, up to a maximum of 24 days per year which may be used for planned time off, subject to approval by the employee's supervisor and HR.
- Sick Leave: All employees are eligible for sick leave from their date of hire, and employees accrue sick leave at a rate of 3 days per month, up to a maximum of 36 days per year. Sick leave may be used for illness, medical appointments, and caring for sick family members.
- Family and Medical Leave: Employees who have worked for at least 6 months are eligible for FMLA leave. FMLA leave provides up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year for qualifying family and medical reasons. FMLA leave may be taken for the birth or adoption of a child, caring for a family member with a serious health condition, or dealing with the employee's own serious health condition.
- Bereavement Leave: All employees are eligible for bereavement leave from their date of hire. Bereavement leave provides up to 2 days of paid leave to attend funeral services and grieve the loss of a family member or loved one.
- Paid Holidays: All employees are eligible for paid holidays from their date of hire and will receive their regular rate of pay for hours not worked on designated holidays.
- Personal Leave: All employees are eligible for personal leave from their date of hire. Personal leave provides up to 2 days of paid leave per year for personal reasons, subject to approval by the employee's supervisor and HR.
- Educational Leave: All employees are eligible for educational leave from their date of hire. Educational leave provides paid time off for employees to attend training programs, pursue academic courses, or obtain certifications relevant to their job responsibilities.
## Leave Request Procedure:
- Employees must request leave in advance, using the company's designated leave request form.
- Leave requests should be submitted to the employee's supervisor and HR for approval.
- HR will review leave requests and communicate approval or denial to the employee and their supervisor.
## Leave Accrual and Carryover:
- Accrued but unused vacation and sick leave may be carried over into the next calendar year, up to a maximum accrual limit of 30 days. Any excess leave beyond the maximum accrual limit will be forfeited unless otherwise approved by HR.
## Leave of Absence:
- Employees may request a leave of absence for extended periods of time beyond available leave balances.
- Leave of absence requests will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis by HR and may be granted for reasons such as medical leave, personal reasons, or educational purposes.
## Return to Work:
- Employees returning from leave are required to provide HR with any necessary documentation related to their leave, such as a doctor's note for medical leave.
- Employees must report to work on their scheduled return date and resume their regular job duties unless otherwise arranged with HR.
## Leave notifications
- Notification of Leave- Staff going on leave are required to notify all Staff of the leave start and end dates via email prior to commencement of the leave. Leave notifications to be sent at least 2 working days prior to the commencement of leave for short leave and at least 5 working days prior to commencement of leave for long leaves.
- Out of Office notification- It is mandatory for office staff to set “Out of Office” reply on emails when on leave, stating the resumption date and the alternate contact person.
## Handover prior to Leave
- It remains the responsibility of every staff to ensure complete handover is done to the replacement staff prior to the commencement of their leave by completing the handover form.
- The only exception to the above rule is Emergency leaves.
## Responsibility and Accountability
- HR Department- HR is responsible for ensuring the principles and parameters of this Policy are followed, and for providing advice regarding the contents of the Leave Policy and Procedure as required. HR is also responsible for raising any concerns regarding unusual Leave patterns identified within their own business area or department.

chapters.title: Training and Development Support:
chapters.text:
- Employees pursuing internal mobility are provided with targeted training, mentorship, and coaching to help them adapt to their new roles effectively. Learning resources are tailored to bridge any skill gaps identified during the transition process.
## Monitoring and Review:
- HR regularly reviews the success of internal mobility programs by tracking the number of internal transfers, promotions, and cross-functional movements. Employee feedback is also gathered to enhance program effectiveness and ensure that opportunities remain equitable and accessible to all
## Educational Assistance:
- To Provide financial support for employees pursuing further education or professional certifications related to their roles or career aspirations. Offer flexible scheduling or remote work options to accommodate employees' educational commitments.
## Performance Feedback, Appraisal and Development Discussions:
- Conduct regular performance evaluations to provide constructive feedback on employees strengths, areas for improvement, and career development progress.
- Facilitate development discussions between managers and employees to set performance goals, create personalized development plans, and track progress over time.
- Performance appraisals are formal evaluations conducted periodically to assess employees job performance, accomplishments, strengths, areas for improvement, and alignment with organizational goals.
- Appraisals are typically conducted by managers or supervisors based on predetermined performance criteria and may include input from employees themselves through self-assessment processes. Performance appraisals are documented and serve as a basis for recognition, rewards, promotions, and performance improvement plans as needed.
## Diversity and Inclusion in Career Advancement
A Packaging Group is committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable workplace where every employee has equal access to opportunities for growth, advancement, and career development. To ensure fairness and transparency, all decisions regarding promotions, skill development, and leadership opportunities are based solely on objective performance criteria, merit, and demonstrated capability, without discrimination of any kind.
To uphold this commitment, the company has established the following actions and safeguards:
Transparent Promotion and Development Criteria:
- Promotion and professional development opportunities are guided by clearly defined criteria, including performance achievements, leadership potential, skill competency, and organizational contribution.
- All employees are informed about promotion eligibility requirements and advancement pathways through periodic communication and performance discussions with their managers.
Regular Review of Promotion and Training Practices:
- HR conducts periodic reviews of promotion and development decisions to ensure they are equitable, merit-based, and aligned with the company’s diversity and inclusion principles. Any identified disparities in advancement opportunities are analyzed and addressed promptly through corrective actions or policy updates.
Anti-Discrimination and DEI Training for HR and Managers:
- All HR personnel and managers involved in performance evaluations, promotions, or training nominations receive regular training on preventing bias, unconscious discrimination, and favoritism.
- These sessions emphasize fair assessment practices, inclusive leadership, and equitable decision-making.
Equal Access to Learning and Skill-Building:
- A Packaging Group ensures that all employees regardless of gender, race, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic have equal access to training programs, workshops, certifications, and professional growth opportunities.
- Employees are encouraged to express career interests and development goals through the annual performance appraisal process.
Accessibility and Support Measures:
- Where needed, the company provides reasonable accommodations (e.g., flexible scheduling, online learning access, or adaptive training materials) to ensure employees with special needs can fully participate in professional development initiatives.
Documentation and Monitoring:
- All promotion and training-related decisions are documented and reviewed by HR to ensure consistency and fairness.
- HR maintains records of participation in training programs and promotion outcomes to monitor trends and confirm that no discriminatory patterns exist across departments or employee groups.
Open Communication and Feedback:
- Employees are encouraged to discuss career aspirations and perceived barriers to advancement with their supervisors or HR.
- Any employee who believes they have been unfairly treated in promotion or development opportunities may raise a concern through the company’s grievance mechanism, which ensures confidentiality and protection from retaliation.

chapters.title: Family-Friendly Programs
chapters.text:
- A Packaging Group provides access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) to support employees and their families with various personal and family-related challenges. The EAP offers confidential counseling services, referrals to community resources, and assistance with family issues such as childcare, parenting, eldercare, and work-life balance.
## Family-Friendly Events and Activities:
- A Packaging Group organizes family-friendly events and activities throughout the year to promote employee well-being and strengthen family bonds. These events may include family picnics, holiday parties, children's day celebrations, and other social gatherings that encourage employees to connect with their families and colleagues in a relaxed and enjoyable atmosphere.

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements:
chapters.text:
- A Packaging Group offers flexible work arrangements to support employees in balancing their work and family responsibilities. This may include options such as telecommuting, flexible hours, compressed workweeks, or job-sharing arrangements. Employees can discuss their individual needs with HR and their supervisors to explore suitable arrangements.
## Parental Leave Policy:
- A Packaging Group provides parental leave to support employees during significant life events such as the birth or adoption of a child. Eligible employees are granted a specified period of paid or unpaid leave to bond with their new child and adjust to their new family dynamics. The parental leave policy applies equally to both mothers and fathers, fostering a supportive and inclusive work environment.
## Childcare Assistance Programs:
- Recognizing the importance of reliable childcare for working parents. A Packaging Group offers childcare assistance programs to help alleviate the financial burden of childcare expenses. These programs may include subsidies, discounts, or reimbursement options for childcare services, ensuring that employees have access to quality childcare while pursuing their careers.

chapters.title: Diversity Policies:
chapters.text:
- A Packaging Group promotes diversity and inclusion in the workplace through formal diversity policies and initiatives. These policies outline our commitment to fostering a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve and ensures equal opportunities for all employees.
## Equal Opportunity and Inclusive Workplace Initiatives
- APackaging Group actively fosters an inclusive workplace where individuals from all backgrounds, abilities, and identities can thrive and contribute to their fullest potential. To translate its diversity commitment into practice, the company implements targeted initiatives and programs that promote equal opportunities and support underrepresented or vulnerable groups within the workforce.
- These initiatives include structured mentorship and peer-support programs designed to help new and minority employees integrate and grow professionally within the organization. The company encourages participation in employee networking and affinity groups that create safe spaces for open dialogue, collaboration, and the celebration of diversity. APG also conducts training sessions and awareness workshops on inclusive behavior, unconscious bias, and equitable treatment to help employees and managers build a culture of respect and empathy.
- Special emphasis is placed on supporting veterans, ethnic minorities, women in leadership roles, and employees with disabilities through targeted development programs, mentorship opportunities, and equitable access to professional growth pathways. All inclusion programs are reviewed periodically by HR to measure impact and ensure continuous improvement.
- Through these ongoing efforts, A Packaging Group reinforces a culture that values diversity, champions equity, and ensures that every employee has a voice and an opportunity to succeed.
## nclusion Programs:
- Inclusion programs at A Packaging Group aim to create a culture of belonging where every employee feels valued, respected, and included. This may include diversity training, employee resource groups, mentorship programs, and initiatives to promote cultural awareness and sensitivity.
## Support and Integration of Differently-Abled Employees
- APackaging Group is dedicated to creating an accessible, equitable, and empowering workplace for employees with disabilities.
- The company recognizes the unique talents and perspectives that individuals with disabilities bring to the organization and is committed to ensuring that all employees can perform their job duties effectively, safely, and with dignity.
- To support the inclusion and participation of employees with disabilities, APackaging Group has implemented the following actions:
- Reasonable Workplace Accommodations:
- The company provides reasonable accommodations based on individual needs, enabling employees with disabilities to perform essential job functions. These accommodations may include ergonomic workstations, assistive devices, modified duties, flexible work schedules, or remote work options where feasible.
- Requests for accommodation can be submitted confidentially to HR and are addressed promptly and respectfully.
- Inclusive Recruitment and Onboarding:
- During recruitment and onboarding, A Packaging Group ensures that job postings, interviews, and induction programs are accessible to all applicants.
- Candidates with disabilities are encouraged to request accommodations for interviews or assessments, and HR ensures equitable consideration based on merit and capability.
- Awareness and Sensitivity Training:
- Regular training sessions are conducted for managers, HR personnel, and employees to build awareness and understanding of disability inclusion. These programs focus on workplace sensitivity, inclusive communication, and the prevention of stigma or unconscious bias toward employees with disabilities.
## Cultural Awareness Training:
- To promote cultural competence and understanding among employees, A Packaging Group offers cultural awareness training programs. These programs provide education and resources to help employees appreciate and respect diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences.
## REVIEW MECHANISM:
At APackaging Group, the HR Manual serves as a comprehensive and evolving guide that defines the company’s people practices, ethical standards, and workplace policies. To ensure that it remains accurate, compliant, and aligned with organizational objectives, the manual undergoes a structured review process led by the Human Resources Department, in collaboration with the Legal, Compliance, and Senior Management teams. This joint effort ensures that all policies and procedures reflect current labor laws, regulatory requirements, and the company’s commitment to fairness and transparency.
